entries.meaning: marks an event or new situation

explanations.title: 人 (rén)
explanations.summary: Can refer to a person or to people; the character itself does not mark singular or plural. 三个人 means three people.

explanations.title: 大 (dà)
explanations.summary: Describes something big or large. In a simple description say 很大, rather than inserting 是 before 大.

explanations.title: 小 (xiǎo)
explanations.summary: Describes something small. Compare 大, big. 小 can also relate to being young in other contexts.

explanations.title: 一 (yī)
explanations.summary: Yī is the dictionary reading and is used in counting. Before a fourth tone it normally becomes yí; before a first, second, or third tone it normally becomes yì.

explanations.title: 二 (èr)
explanations.summary: Use 二 when counting or reading digits. Before most classifiers, 两 is normally used instead: 两个人 means two people.

explanations.title: 三 (sān)
explanations.summary: First tone: high and level. 三个人 means three people.

explanations.title: 日 (rì)
explanations.summary: A character used for sun or day, especially in compounds and written dates. For the sun in ordinary conversation, 太阳 is usual; 天 is common when counting days.

explanations.title: 月 (yuè)
explanations.summary: In dates, a number plus 月 names the month: 三月 is March. 月 also means moon; everyday speech often uses 月亮 for the moon.

explanations.title: 水 (shuǐ)
explanations.summary: 喝水 means drink water. The final ui is written with the tone mark on i: shuǐ.

explanations.title: 火 (huǒ)
explanations.summary: Means fire and appears in many compounds. Its third tone is often low in connected speech.

explanations.title: 山 (shān)
explanations.summary: An everyday noun meaning mountain. The first tone stays high and level.

explanations.title: 木 (mù)
explanations.summary: A character meaning wood or tree, often used inside compounds. 树 is the usual everyday word for a tree.

explanations.title: 口 (kǒu)
explanations.summary: Can mean mouth or an opening. 嘴 is also common for mouth in conversation; 口 occurs in many compounds and counting expressions.

explanations.title: 天 (tiān)
explanations.summary: Can mean day or sky. 三天 means three days; 今天 means today.

explanations.title: 好 (hǎo)
explanations.summary: Use hǎo for good or well. 好 also has the reading hào in other words, so its pronunciation depends on meaning.

explanations.title: 我 (wǒ)
explanations.summary: Use 我 for yourself. Chinese pronouns do not change form between I and me.

explanations.title: 你 (nǐ)
explanations.summary: The usual singular you. 您 (nín) is a more respectful form.

explanations.title: 他 (tā)
explanations.summary: Written 他 refers to he or him. It sounds exactly like 她 (she/her), so speech needs context.

explanations.title: 她 (tā)
explanations.summary: Written 她 refers to she or her. It sounds exactly like 他 (he/him); the 女 component helps distinguish the writing.

explanations.title: 女 (nǚ)
explanations.summary: A character meaning female or woman. 女人 and 女性 are fuller words; 女 also appears as a component in other characters.

explanations.title: 子 (zǐ)
explanations.summary: A character meaning child or son in some words. Everyday child is usually 孩子. 子 has the dictionary reading zǐ, but is neutral in common words such as 孩子 and 名字.

explanations.title: 中 (zhōng)
explanations.summary: Zhōng means middle or center and appears in 中国 (China). China is not the meaning of 中 in every context. The character also has the reading zhòng in other uses.

explanations.title: 国 (guó)
explanations.summary: Means country or state, usually inside a compound such as 中国 or 国家. Do not replace the full country name 中国 with 国 alone.

explanations.title: 是 (shì)
explanations.summary: Links a person or thing to an identity or category: 我是学生 means I am a student. It is not a general equivalent of English yes or the is before an adjective.

explanations.title: 不 (bù)
explanations.summary: Usually negates present or habitual actions and descriptions. Before a fourth-tone syllable it is normally pronounced bú. Negate 有 with 没有 instead.

explanations.title: 四 (sì)
explanations.summary: Fourth tone: a clear fall. 四 (sì) and 十 (shí, ten) have different initials and tones.

explanations.title: 五 (wǔ)
explanations.summary: Third tone. In ordinary speech a third tone is often low rather than a full dip and rise.

explanations.title: 六 (liù)
explanations.summary: Fourth tone. 六个人 means six people.

explanations.title: 八 (bā)
explanations.summary: First tone. 八个人 means eight people.

explanations.title: 十 (shí)
explanations.summary: 十一 means eleven and 二十 means twenty. 十 and 石 (stone) are pronounced alike.

explanations.title: 九 (jiǔ)
explanations.summary: Third tone. 九 comes between 八 (eight) and 十 (ten) when counting.

explanations.title: 上 (shàng)
explanations.summary: Can mean above or up. It also has other uses in phrases such as 上学, go to school.

explanations.title: 下 (xià)
explanations.summary: Can mean below or down. It also has other uses, so the whole phrase determines the meaning.

explanations.title: 手 (shǒu)
explanations.summary: Means hand. It also appears in 手机 (mobile phone), where translating each character separately does not give the whole word's meaning.

explanations.title: 目 (mù)
explanations.summary: A character meaning eye, mostly used in compounds. The ordinary conversational word for eye is 眼睛 (yǎnjing). 目 and 木 sound alike.

explanations.title: 田 (tián)
explanations.summary: Usually refers to cultivated land, especially in compounds. It is useful character knowledge but not a priority for the first conversational lessons.

explanations.title: 石 (shí)
explanations.summary: A character meaning stone, commonly used in compounds. 石头 (shítou) is an everyday word for a stone. 石 also has another reading in a traditional unit of measure.

explanations.title: 门 (mén)
explanations.summary: An everyday noun meaning door or gate. It has a rising second tone.

explanations.title: 车 (chē)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for a vehicle or car. The character has the reading jū in some specialized contexts, such as Chinese chess.

explanations.title: 马 (mǎ)
explanations.summary: An everyday noun meaning horse. Its third tone is different from the neutral tone of the question particle 吗.

explanations.title: 鸟 (niǎo)
explanations.summary: An everyday noun meaning bird. Its third tone is often low in connected speech.

explanations.title: 鱼 (yú)
explanations.summary: An everyday noun meaning fish, including fish as food. It has a rising second tone.

explanations.title: 米 (mǐ)
explanations.summary: Commonly means uncooked rice or rice grain. 米饭 is the ordinary word for cooked rice; 米 can also mean meter as a unit of length.

explanations.title: 父 (fù)
explanations.summary: A character meaning father, usually in compounds such as 父亲. 爸爸 is the everyday beginner word for dad.

explanations.title: 母 (mǔ)
explanations.summary: A character meaning mother, usually in compounds such as 母亲. 妈妈 is the everyday beginner word for mom.

explanations.title: 家 (jiā)
explanations.summary: Can mean home or family. 回家 means return home; 家 does not only refer to the physical building.

explanations.title: 学 (xué)
explanations.summary: Can mean to learn or study. 学习 is a common fuller word; 学 also appears in 学生 and 学校.

explanations.title: 生 (shēng)
explanations.summary: A character with several meanings, including life, being born, and raw. Learn its meaning in complete words; 学生 means student, not study-life.

explanations.title: 年 (nián)
explanations.summary: Use 年 for years and dates. For a person's age in years, use 岁 instead.

explanations.title: 你好 (nǐ hǎo)
explanations.summary: A common greeting. Both syllables are written with third tones; in ordinary speech the first changes to a rising tone: ní hǎo.

explanations.title: 谢谢 (xièxie)
explanations.summary: Use to thank someone. The second syllable is neutral and usually shorter and lighter than the first.

explanations.title: 朋友 (péngyou)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for friend. The second syllable, you, is neutral: péngyou.

explanations.title: 今天 (jīntiān)
explanations.summary: Both syllables have first tone. 今天 is today, 昨天 yesterday, and 明天 tomorrow.

explanations.title: 学校 (xuéxiào)
explanations.summary: A place of education. The tones are second then fourth.

explanations.title: 喜欢 (xǐhuan)
explanations.summary: Can be followed by a noun or an activity: 喜欢茶 means like tea; 喜欢看书 means like reading. The second syllable, huan, is neutral.

explanations.title: 妈妈 (māma)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for mother. The first syllable has first tone and the second is neutral.

explanations.title: 谁 (shéi)
explanations.summary: Asks which person is meant. Shéi and shuí are both accepted pronunciations of this word.

explanations.title: 看 (kàn)
explanations.summary: Use kàn for looking, watching, or reading. 看书 means read a book. 看 also has the reading kān for guarding or looking after.

explanations.title: 看 (kān)
explanations.summary: Use kān for guarding or looking after, as in 看门 (kān mén). This is a different reading of the same character as kàn, look/watch/read.

explanations.title: 吗 (ma)
explanations.summary: At the end of a statement, 吗 makes a yes/no question. This particle is neutral tone; do not add it automatically to questions already containing 什么 or 谁.

explanations.title: 的 (de)
explanations.summary: Links an owner or description to a noun: 我的书 means my book. This grammatical use is neutral de; the character has other readings in other words.

explanations.title: 了 (le)
explanations.summary: Neutral le is used after verbs for completed events or at sentence end for a new situation. It is not a general past-tense ending; other words use the reading liǎo.

explanations.title: 再见 (zàijiàn)
explanations.summary: A common way to say goodbye. Both syllables have fourth tones.

explanations.title: 请 (qǐng)
explanations.summary: Before an action, 请 makes a polite request. 请坐 (qǐng zuò) means please sit down.

explanations.title: 对不起 (duìbuqǐ)
explanations.summary: Use to apologize or politely get someone's attention. In this expression, bu is neutral; it is not the ordinary isolated reading bù.

explanations.title: 您 (nín)
explanations.summary: A respectful singular form of you, often used with elders, customers, or someone you wish to address politely.

explanations.title: 也 (yě)
explanations.summary: Usually comes before the verb or adjective phrase. 我也去 means I am going too.

explanations.title: 很 (hěn)
explanations.summary: Often comes before an adjective. In an ordinary description it may simply make the sentence natural, without strongly emphasizing very.

explanations.title: 叫 (jiào)
explanations.summary: Use 我叫... to give your name. 叫 also means to call or shout in other contexts.

explanations.title: 名字 (míngzi)
explanations.summary: Means a person's or thing's name. The second syllable, zi, is neutral.

explanations.title: 什么 (shénme)
explanations.summary: Use to ask what something is or what someone does or wants. The second syllable, me, is neutral. 什么 stays where the answer would go in the sentence.

explanations.title: 哪 (nǎ)
explanations.summary: Asks which one. 哪个 (nǎ ge) means which one; 哪 is different from 那 (nà, that).

explanations.title: 零 (líng)
explanations.summary: Use 零 for zero, including when reading digits in a phone number. It has a second tone.

explanations.title: 个 (gè)
explanations.summary: A common counting word between a number and a noun: 三个人 means three people. Its dictionary tone is fourth; it is often neutral in phrases such as 一个 (yí ge).

explanations.title: 两 (liǎng)
explanations.summary: Normally used before classifiers: 两个人 means two people. Use 二 for counting one, two, three and for most digit-by-digit numbers.

explanations.title: 有 (yǒu)
explanations.summary: Expresses possession or existence. 我有书 means I have a book or books. Its usual negative is 没有, not 不有.

explanations.title: 没有 (méiyǒu)
explanations.summary: Negates 有: 我没有书 means I do not have a book. It can also negate an action that has not happened; start with possession here.

explanations.title: 爸爸 (bàba)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for father. The first syllable has fourth tone and the second is neutral.

explanations.title: 哥哥 (gēge)
explanations.summary: Refers to an older brother. Chinese distinguishes older and younger siblings; the second syllable is neutral.

explanations.title: 姐姐 (jiějie)
explanations.summary: Refers to an older sister. The second syllable is neutral.

explanations.title: 弟弟 (dìdi)
explanations.summary: Refers to a younger brother. Compare 哥哥, older brother. The second syllable is neutral.

explanations.title: 妹妹 (mèimei)
explanations.summary: Refers to a younger sister. Compare 姐姐, older sister. The second syllable is neutral.

explanations.title: 孩子 (háizi)
explanations.summary: The usual everyday word for a child or children. The second syllable is neutral; 子 alone is not the ordinary conversational substitute.

explanations.title: 想 (xiǎng)
explanations.summary: Before an action, 想 can express wanting to do it. 想喝茶 means want to drink tea. It can also mean think or miss someone.

explanations.title: 要 (yào)
explanations.summary: Expresses wanting or needing something. 我要茶 means I want tea; 想 often sounds softer when expressing a wish to do something.

explanations.title: 吃 (chī)
explanations.summary: Use for eating. 吃饭 (chīfàn) means to eat or have a meal; it does not require the meal to contain rice.

explanations.title: 喝 (hē)
explanations.summary: Use with drinks: 喝水 means drink water. The reading taught here is hē; 喝 has another reading in other uses.

explanations.title: 茶 (chá)
explanations.summary: 喝茶 means drink tea. 茶 has a rising second tone.

explanations.title: 咖啡 (kāfēi)
explanations.summary: Both syllables have first tone. 喝咖啡 means drink coffee.

explanations.title: 米饭 (mǐfàn)
explanations.summary: The ordinary word for cooked rice as food. Compare 米, which commonly refers to uncooked rice.

explanations.title: 菜 (cài)
explanations.summary: Can mean vegetables or a prepared dish. A 菜 can contain meat; it does not always mean a vegetable dish.

explanations.title: 来 (lái)
explanations.summary: Often describes movement toward the speaker or the relevant place. Compare 去, go.

explanations.title: 去 (qù)
explanations.summary: Use before a destination: 去学校 means go to school. Compare 来, come.

explanations.title: 回 (huí)
explanations.summary: 回家 means return home. 回 can also mean reply in other contexts.

explanations.title: 在 (zài)
explanations.summary: Use to give a location: 我在家 means I am at home. Before an action, 在 can also mark that it is in progress.

explanations.title: 这里 (zhèlǐ)
explanations.summary: Refers to this place. 我在这里 means I am here. 这儿 is another common form, not included as a separate entry in this course.

explanations.title: 明天 (míngtiān)
explanations.summary: The day after today. 明 has second tone and 天 has first tone.

explanations.title: 昨天 (zuótiān)
explanations.summary: The day before today. 昨 has second tone and 天 has first tone.

explanations.title: 现在 (xiànzài)
explanations.summary: Refers to the present time. Both syllables have fourth tone.

explanations.title: 时候 (shíhou)
explanations.summary: Used in 什么时候 (shénme shíhou), meaning when. It is not the word for an hour; hou is neutral.

explanations.title: 星期 (xīngqī)
explanations.summary: 星期一 through 星期六 name Monday through Saturday. Sunday is 星期日 or 星期天.

explanations.title: 点 (diǎn)
explanations.summary: After a number, 点 gives the hour: 三点 means three o'clock. It has several other meanings, including point or dot.

explanations.title: 多 (duō)
explanations.summary: Describes a large quantity. 很多 means many or a lot; compare 少, few or little.

explanations.title: 少 (shǎo)
explanations.summary: Describes a small quantity. This meaning is shǎo; shào belongs to other uses of the character.

explanations.title: 热 (rè)
explanations.summary: Can describe hot weather or feeling hot. Compare 冷, cold.

explanations.title: 冷 (lěng)
explanations.summary: Can describe cold weather or feeling cold. Compare 热, hot.

explanations.title: 忙 (máng)
explanations.summary: 我很忙 means I am busy. 很 can make a simple description natural without strongly emphasizing very.

explanations.title: 累 (lèi)
explanations.summary: Use lèi when describing tiredness. 累 has different readings in other words; learn this reading with its meaning.

explanations.title: 高兴 (gāoxìng)
explanations.summary: Expresses happiness or pleasure. The tones are first then fourth.

explanations.title: 学生 (xuésheng)
explanations.summary: Student. CC-CEDICT records xuésheng with neutral sheng; the official 2025 HSK syllabus gives xuéshēng. Both are accepted here. Do not confuse 学生 with 老师 (teacher).

explanations.title: 老师 (lǎoshī)
explanations.summary: An everyday word and form of address for a teacher. Do not pronounce the second syllable like the neutral sheng in 学生.

explanations.title: 学习 (xuéxí)
explanations.summary: Used for learning or studying. 学习汉语 means study Chinese.

explanations.title: 汉语 (hànyǔ)
explanations.summary: Refers to the Chinese language. In this course the spoken variety taught is standard Mandarin; 中文 is another common term for Chinese.

explanations.title: 听 (tīng)
explanations.summary: Use for listening or hearing. 听老师说 means listen to the teacher speak.

explanations.title: 说 (shuō)
explanations.summary: Use for speaking or saying something. 说汉语 means speak Chinese.

explanations.title: 读 (dú)
explanations.summary: Can mean reading silently or aloud. 看书 is also used for reading, so 看 and 读 are not always contrasting answers.

explanations.title: 写 (xiě)
explanations.summary: 写字 means to write characters. The tone mark goes on e in xiě.

explanations.title: 书 (shū)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for book. 看书 means read a book; use 本 as the classifier when counting books.

explanations.title: 字 (zì)
explanations.summary: A written character, as in 汉字. A Chinese word may contain one character or several characters.

explanations.title: 这 (zhè)
explanations.summary: Points to something nearby or being discussed. Compare 那, that. Before classifiers you may also hear zhèi.

explanations.title: 那 (nà)
explanations.summary: Points to something farther away or already mentioned. Compare 这, this. Before classifiers you may also hear nèi.

explanations.title: 钱 (qián)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for money. 多少钱 means how much money or how much does it cost.

explanations.title: 买 (mǎi)
explanations.summary: Third tone. Do not confuse 买 (buy) with 卖 (mài, sell), which has a different tone and an extra part at the top.

explanations.title: 多少 (duōshao)
explanations.summary: Asks about an amount or number. 多少钱 asks the price. The second syllable, shao, is neutral in this question word as taught here.

explanations.title: 商店 (shāngdiàn)
explanations.summary: A place where things are sold. The tones are first then fourth.

explanations.title: 块 (kuài)
explanations.summary: In everyday price expressions, 块 is the spoken unit for yuan: 三块钱 means three yuan. It also counts pieces or chunks of things.
